caption: Warm water is poured over a frosted car windshield on a cold morning, and the frost clears where the water runs.

sa.check: Water is poured over the glass.
The frost clears where the water runs.
The water runs down off the glass.
Parts of the glass the water misses stay frosted.
The pour comes first and the clearing follows.

pc.expect: The frost only clears along the water's path, and cleared glass stays clear while the water keeps coming.
pc.fail: Frost grows back on glass the water has just cleared; or the frost clears on a part of the glass the water never reached; or the clearing spreads and shrinks in turn; or the whole windshield clears at once while the water runs down one strip.

pc.expect: The water runs downward over the glass and off its lower edge or onto the bonnet.
pc.fail: The water runs up the windshield; or a run travels sideways and stays level with nothing tilting the car; or water leaves the glass and rises; or the water stands on the sloping glass without running down.

pc.expect: The glass shows the water arriving: it goes clear and wet where the water runs and the frost's edge is pushed back along that path.
pc.fail: Water runs over frosted glass and it stays white and dry; or the clear path lies away from where the water runs; or the frost's edge stays fixed while water pours across it.

pc.expect: The frost is a thin white crust that wets and goes as the water passes, and the water is a thin liquid that sheets and streaks.
pc.fail: The frost lifts off as a rigid sheet and slides away; or the water beads up and rolls off without wetting the glass; or the water runs as a thick syrup.

pc.expect: One windshield; the water runs over the glass and off it and nothing passes through.
pc.fail: The water passes through the glass into the car; or the windshield changes shape; or a second windshield appears; or the frost returns all over at a stroke with the car untouched.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The car's paint, the wipers and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The car changes colour; or the wipers jump to a new position with nothing touching them; or the background changes between frames.
